new_entities.name: School-based mindfulness intervention
new_entities.description: Mindfulness-based programs delivered in school settings to children or adolescents.

new_entities.name: Child anxiety symptoms
new_entities.description: Anxiety symptoms or anxiety/stress scales measured in children and adolescents.

edges.effect_quant: A 2019 meta-analysis of 33 randomized trials involving 3,666 children and adolescents found small but statistically significant benefits of mindfulness-based interventions for anxiety/stress, with effect sizes in the d=0.16 to 0.30 range overall, but effects were less consistent in the active-control subset.
edges.population: school-age children and adolescents exposed to mindfulness programs in classroom or school-linked settings
edges.mechanism: Mindfulness training may improve attention regulation, stress appraisal, and emotional awareness, which can reduce anxious arousal for some students.
edges.summary: School-based mindfulness interventions can modestly reduce anxiety symptoms in some child and adolescent groups, but the effects are heterogeneous and not consistently robust across trials or comparators.
edges.caveats: Benefits tend to be small, vary by age and implementation quality, and are less convincing against active controls. Some school mindfulness programs improve broader well-being or stress regulation more reliably than anxiety-specific endpoints.

evidence.citation: Dunning DL et al 2019 J Child Psychol Psychiatry
evidence.notes: Research Review: The effects of mindfulness-based interventions on cognition and mental health in children and adolescents - a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
